in_arabic.name: مُتَوَلّى
in_arabic.long_meaning: المُتَوَلّى هو اللّاحِقُ بالسِمعَة وَالإع تِراف، وَالسِمعَة هي الرَغبة بالدُنيا، والإع تِراف هو الإِحاطَة بالعِباد وَالأَشخاص. وَاللّاحِق بهما هو الجَزيلُ العَظيمُ، والذى يحظى بهما هو المُتَوَلّى. وَهو من أَعظم الأَسامي في الإسلام، وَكثير من الأَئِمَّة وَالسلاطين حَملوا هذا الأَسَمُ في سِيرتهم. ومِن أَنواع المُتَوَلّى المُتَوَلّى بالخُلَفاء، المُتَوَلّى بالعِلم، والمُتَوَلّى بالفُضْل، والمُتَوَلّى بالأَعمار، والمُتَوَلّى بِالنّواميس

in_urdu.name: مُتَوَلّى
in_urdu.meaning: وہ شخص جو دنیا کی خواہش اور لوگوں کے ساتھ رشتہ داری میں فائز ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: مُتَوَلّی وہ ہے جس کے پاس دنیا کی خواہش اور لوگوں کے ساتھ رشتہ داری کی زیادہ مقدار ہوتی ہے. یہ ایک اسلامی نام ہے جس کا تعلق کثرت اور عظمت سے ہے. اور کہا جاتا ہے کہ یہ نام کئی اہم اسلامی ناموں اور سلطانوں میں سے ایک ہے. مُتَوَلّی کے معنی میں شامل ہیں: مُتَوَلّی خُلَفاء, مُتَوَلّی علم, مُتَوَلّی فضل, مُتَوَلّی عمر, مُتَوَلّی نوامیس

It is a name that connotes grandeur, magnificence, and abundance. In Islamic tradition, Mutawalli is considered a name of great significance, associated with numerous prominent Islamic leaders and personalities throughout history. The term Mutawalli is derived from the Arabic root 'w-l-l', which means to possess or have abundance of something. In Islamic theology, the term is used to describe one who has a deep understanding of the faith and is blessed with spiritual insight. Mutawalli's name is often associated with desirable qualities such as intelligence, wisdom, and compassion. In modern times, the name Mutawalli has been adopted by various Muslim cultures, symbolizing the values of Islamic virtues and character.

data.cultural_impact: The title "Mutawalli" holds significant importance in the Islamic finance industry as it refers to the trustee or custodian of the funds or assets. In the context of modern Islamic finance, a Mutawalli assumes the role of maintaining and managing Shariah-compliant investment portfolios based on the principles of Islamic law.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the title "Mutawalli" goes beyond the realm of Islamic finance and resonates with deeper intentions and personal values. A person who is referred to as a Mutawalli is often viewed as someone who exercises stewardship and takes care of the trusts (awqaf) placed upon them – money, resources or even knowledge. According to Islamic teachings, this role of a Mutawalli finds a parallel in the concept of khilafa (trusteeship) bestowed upon every human by Allah, who is the ultimate owner of all creation. Therefore, the title "Mutawalli" serves as a reminder of our collective responsibility to act as caretakers not only of our physical and material possessions, but also of our spiritual and moral reserves.

historical_references.reference: The Mutawalli was an office in the Islamic caliphate responsible for managing the waqf properties and income.
historical_references.context: During the Islamic Golden Age, the waqf system emerged as a significant means of charitable giving and economic investment. The Mutawalli, or custodian, was appointed to manage these properties and the income generated from them, ensuring that the funds were used in accordance with the founder's wishes and for the benefit of the community.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The Mutawalli played an essential role in the administration of the Ottoman Empire's vast waqfs. The name Mutawalli carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: As the Ottoman Empire expanded, the waqf system became increasingly important for the economic development and social welfare of its subjects. The Mutawalli's role in managing these properties and their income helped to foster stability and prosperity in the empire, making it one of the most powerful and influential in history.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Mutawalli' is derived from the Arabic word 'Walaa' which means 'loyalty' or 'affection'. In Islamic finance, a Mutawalli is an intermediary or trustee who manages and safeguards the assets of an Islamic investment fund. In the context of real estate management, a Mutawalli is appointed by an Islamic mortgagee to manage and maintain the property until the mortgage debt is repaid. In corporate governance, a Mutawalli is a supervisory board member who ensures that the company's activities comply with Sharia law. The use of Mutawallis is becoming increasingly popular on various platforms including Islamic banks, property management companies, and corporate entities, as they provide assurance to investors and stakeholders that the financial and ethical obligations of the investment or enterprise are being met in accordance with Islamic law.
